title: Derived Classes and Access Modes
learningObjectives: Explain derived classes and access modes.
Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Inheritance access mode affects how inherited public and protected members are exposed in the derived type. Private base members remain inaccessible directly to derived code.
understand.whyItMatters: Access modes control the interface of the derived type.
understand.explain: Know public/protected/private inheritance behavior and avoid inheritance solely to expose internals.

examples.title: Public inheritance
examples.code: class Base{public:void show(){};protected:int x=1;};\nclass Derived:public Base{};\nDerived d;d.show();
examples.explanation: Public base interface stays public in derived.

examples.title: Protected inheritance
examples.code: class Base{public:void f(){};protected:int value=2;};\nclass Derived:protected Base{};
examples.explanation: Base public/protected members become protected in Derived.

examples.title: Private inheritance
examples.code: class Base{public:void f(){};protected:int x=0;};\nclass Derived:private Base{};
examples.explanation: Inherited public and protected members become private in Derived.

examples.title: Base private remains private
examples.code: class Base{private:int secret=1;protected:int safe=2;};\nclass Derived:public Base{void use(){safe=3;}};
examples.explanation: Derived cannot access base private member secret.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Derived Classes and Access Modes examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating derived classes and access modes in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

questions.prompt: Public inheritance keeps base public as?
Protected inheritance turns base public into?
Private inheritance turns inherited public into?
Can derived access base private field?
questions.explanation: Base private members are inaccessible directly.
